topic: bangladesh conducts first-ever survey of ethnic minorities
headline_marked: BBS launches [[first-ever survey of ethnic minorities]] to map socioeconomic status
headline: BBS launches first-ever survey of ethnic minorities to map socioeconomic status
summary: The Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics is collecting data on 50 different ethnic groups to determine poverty rates and improve living standards.
details: The Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) has launched the country's first-ever survey to assess the living standards and poverty levels of ethnic minority communities. The nationwide survey began on October 1 and is scheduled to run until October 25.

The survey aims to create a comprehensive list of ethnic minority families and gather detailed socioeconomic data. This will help the BBS identify which communities are most lagging behind and which are progressing, allowing for targeted poverty reduction and development plans.

The questionnaire includes 50 different ethnic minority groups, while the Bengali population is excluded from this specific study. To ensure cultural sensitivity and accuracy, the BBS has hired enumerators from within these ethnic communities, including young students.
BBS officials noted that since Bengali speakers may not fully grasp the language, culture, and social realities of these groups, hiring community members was essential for effective data collection.

However, the process has faced some resistance. Enumerators reported embarrassing situations in Dhaka, Chattogram, and Mymensingh, where some residents were reluctant to provide information or questioned the purpose of the survey.

Project Director Farhana Sultana told Prothom Alo that while some faced hurdles, they were were able to convince residents that the data is being collected for their own future development. She urged all ethnic minority communities to cooperate with the survey.

The project will create a benchmark database to monitor changes in living standards and evaluate the progress of development activities over time. It also aims to collect disaggregated data for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to ensure 'no one is left behind'.

The total cost of the project is estimated at 28 crore BDT, with the project term ending on June 30, 2028. The final results will provide a full picture of poverty rates and living standards among ethnic minorities in Bangladesh.
caption:

topic: three tourists die, two missing after swimming in Cox's Bazar sea
headline_marked: 3 tourists [[die, 2 missing]] after swimming in Cox’s Bazar
headline: 3 tourists die, 2 missing after swimming in Cox’s Bazar
summary: The tragedy occurred on Wednesday evening at Himchhari beach, involving tourists from Chattogram and Dhaka.
details: Three tourists died after going for a swim in the sea off Himchhari in Cox’s Bazar, while two others remain missing.
The incident happened around 5:00 PM on Wednesday at the beach adjacent to the Marina Resort museum in Himchhari.
According to Dolon Acharya, senior station officer of Cox’s Bazar Fire Service and Civil Defence, two groups of tourists were involved.
One group of visitors came from the Bayezid area of Chattogram, while the other group hailed from Uttara in Dhaka.
Rescue teams recovered three bodies from the sea, while one other tourist was rescued alive.
The rescued individual has been admitted to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital for treatment.
Authorities have not yet confirmed the identities of the deceased, the missing, or the rescued person.
